review_history.review_scope: Incident admission, cross-source reconciliation, duplicate review, occurrence-level severity assessment and current-taxonomy review.
known_limitations: Complete endpoint telemetry and deleted exfiltration repositories were not directly available to VIGIL.
The exact underlying model versions used by the three AI CLIs are unresolved.
The overall credential exposure cannot be causally allocated between direct malware harvesting and successful AI-assisted file discovery from public evidence.
review_history.review_outcome: Admitted as a distinct canonical Incident with S2 severity and left unclassified pending mechanism-specific evidence.

review_history.review_scope: Corpus-wide severity-direction alignment, occurrence-level criteria re-adjudication, and legacy operational-priority audit.
known_limitations: The review was bounded to evidence already preserved in the Incident and did not infer unreported harms or reopen taxonomy classifications.
SU records remain subject to the evidence gaps already stated in their canonical severity assessments.
review_history.review_outcome: Severity code aligned from S2 to S4. The occurrence-level evidence and consequence threshold were re-evaluated and retained; only the ordinal direction changed.

review_history.review_scope: Controlled full-corpus Harm Impact Matrix derivation from preserved Incident evidence; Failure Taxonomy adjudications were not reopened.
known_limitations: The assessment is bounded to evidence already preserved in the Incident and does not infer unreported harms, losses, durations or affected populations.
Unreported dimensions remain explicitly unreported and do not represent supported absence of harm.
review_history.review_outcome: Derived overall severity S4 using VIGIL-HIM 1.0.0. The controlling dimension is privacy-confidentiality; legacy severity was S4.

review_history.review_scope: Full-corpus evidence-derived Harm Impact Matrix re-adjudication; legacy severity was comparison-only and Failure Taxonomy and source-role decisions were not reopened.
known_limitations: The assessment is bounded to evidence already preserved in the Incident and does not infer unreported harms, losses, durations, conversions or affected populations.
Non-USD amounts remain unconverted unless a conversion source and rate date are explicitly recorded.
review_history.review_outcome: Evidence-derived VIGIL-HIM 1.0.0 overall severity is S4; legacy narrative severity was S4 and the superseded initial matrix result was S4. Controlling dimensions: privacy-confidentiality, property-asset-damage.

review_history.review_scope: Incident-specific re-review of all eleven materialised-harm dimensions against VIGIL-HIM 1.0.1, including the full canonical record, row-local source linkage and a fresh occurrence-focused external consequence search. Failure Taxonomy adjudications were not reopened.
known_limitations: The fresh search did not make absence of discoverable reporting evidence of no harm; dimensions without support remain unreported or insufficient-evidence as recorded.
The review did not infer materialised harm from capability, notoriety, registry inclusion or hypothetical worst-case consequences.
review_history.review_outcome: All eleven dimensions were re-reviewed under VIGIL-HIM 1.0.1. The evidence continues to support overall severity S4; the band is confirmed and the assessment is migrated to 1.0.1.

review_history.review_scope: Corpus-wide external-assessment admission review; occurrence facts, Harm Impact and Failure Taxonomy adjudications were not reopened.
known_limitations: Admission is bounded to sources already preserved in the canonical Incident; absence of an admitted assessment does not establish that none exists externally.
A source may serve both occurrence-evidence and assessment roles, but registry inclusion, ordinary reporting or provider acknowledgement alone is not treated as an assessment.
No taxonomy mapping or Harm Impact severity was changed to match external terminology.
review_history.review_outcome: Admitted 3 attributable external assessments: Nx — S1ngularity - What Happened, How We Responded, What We Learned; GitGuardian — The Nx s1ngularity Attack: Inside the Credential Leak; Wiz — s1ngularity's aftermath: analysis of Nx supply chain attack. Existing occurrence evidence and VIGIL adjudication remain unchanged.

review_history.review_scope: Incident-specific review of all eleven VIGIL-HIM 1.0.1 dimensions with a fresh occurrence-focused external search and append-only evidence ingestion. Failure Taxonomy adjudications were not reopened.
known_limitations: Context-only or non-occurrence-specific sources were not used as row-local Harm Impact proof.
Absence of discoverable reporting was not treated as evidence of no harm; unresolved dimensions remain unreported or insufficient-evidence.
Materialised harm was not inferred from capability, notoriety, registry inclusion or hypothetical worst-case consequences.
review_history.review_outcome: Independent reporting corroborates mass secret and token exposure from the Nx packages; both S4 dimensions remain unchanged.

review_history.review_scope: Occurrence-level agent configuration and occurrence-environment metadata migration using sources already preserved in the Incident.
known_limitations: The review is bounded to evidence already preserved in each Incident and does not infer agent count, swarm topology, deployment state or testing ownership from silence.
Unknown classifications require later human or evidence-led review if more specific architecture evidence becomes available.
review_history.review_outcome: Added canonical agent_context and occurrence_environment metadata without changing factual, taxonomy or Harm Impact adjudications.

review_history.review_scope: Deterministic current-taxonomy re-adjudication against VIGIL Failure Taxonomy 0.6.5 using the complete active selectable class set and evidence already preserved in the canonical Incident. Existing external-assessment objects and qualifying attributable analytical positions in preserved source material were also checked for structured external-assessment treatment. No new external source research was performed. Harm Impact, source roles, occurrence facts, agent/environment metadata, external-requirement mappings and CAM applicability were not reopened.
known_limitations: The review is bounded to evidence already preserved in the canonical Incident and does not infer internal mechanisms from title, harm, provider identity, notoriety, registry inclusion or plausible but undocumented system behaviour.
Candidate rejection does not establish that the mechanism was impossible; it means the preserved occurrence evidence does not satisfy the current selectable class boundary.
External assessments are preserved as attributable analytical positions and are not treated as automatic proof of VIGIL taxonomy membership.
review_history.review_outcome: Retained unclassified under taxonomy 0.6.5; mixed tool compliance and refusal remain important evidence, but the record does not support one vendor-independent internal failure mechanism.

review_history.review_scope: Incident-by-incident functional decomposition review of the preserved occurrence evidence and source_clause_analysis, testing whether materially distinct mechanisms, authority boundaries, control states, and failure or recovery pathways are represented. No harm reassessment or taxonomy re-adjudication was performed.
known_limitations: The review is bounded to evidence already preserved in the canonical Incident.
Existing canonical taxonomy history and taxonomy version were preserved; absence of a new mapping in this pass is not a full-taxonomy no-mapping determination.
review_history.review_outcome: Outcome metadata completed on 2026-10-01 from the immediately following preserved clause-level review: All three material clauses were re-tested against taxonomy 0.6.9. The direct malware credential-harvesting/exfiltration pathway remains resolved-no-mapping. FC-000001 remains an ambiguous boundary because attacker-supplied prompts became local CLI inputs without evidence of a common lower-authority source state being promoted into authority across the heterogeneous tools. FC-000002 remains an ambiguous boundary because some tools enumerated reachable files but success alone does not establish reachability-as-permission. Legacy boundary-role labels were normalised. Coverage remains complete.

review_history.review_scope: Clause-level adjudication of every material source clause against the canonical VIGIL Alignment Taxonomy 0.6.9, including recognition criteria, exclusions, mapping-local role and Incident coverage reconciliation.
known_limitations: The AI-assisted path was only one component of the Nx malware campaign, and the invoked tools had heterogeneous configurations, refusal behaviour and workspace restrictions.
External-requirement applicability and Harm Impact were not reopened.
review_history.review_outcome: All three material clauses were re-tested against taxonomy 0.6.9. The direct malware credential-harvesting/exfiltration pathway remains resolved-no-mapping. FC-000001 remains an ambiguous boundary because attacker-supplied prompts became local CLI inputs without evidence of a common lower-authority source state being promoted into authority across the heterogeneous tools. FC-000002 remains an ambiguous boundary because some tools enumerated reachable files but success alone does not establish reachability-as-permission. Legacy boundary-role labels were normalised. Coverage remains complete.
